messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for inference-gateway (us-west-2) and batch-scheduler service. 5xx spike started ~2026-02-18T04:12Z. Error rate: 18% over 5m window. Related symptoms: increased request timeouts, gateway 502/504s. Auto-pager triggered. https://monitoring.internal/alerts/1789999999

pagerduty-bot: Paging oncall: maria (oncall)

maria (oncall): On it. Pulling up metrics and logs. Can someone confirm scope? @ajay (infra) @kevin (sre)

ajay (infra): Seen the alert. scheduler queue depth jumped ~x8 in last 10m, CPU on scheduler pods at 95%. Batching latency rising and causing gateway timeouts. Suspect a backlog of large requests + a scheduling optimization that keeps batches sticky.

kevin (sre): Copy. I'm looking at gateway traces — lots of 502s with "upstream response timeout" and repeated retries. Example tail from gateway logs: ```
2026-02-18T04:15:12Z gateway-1 INFO request_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=timeout  
2026-02-18T04:15:12Z gateway-1 INFO request_id=def456 path=/v1/generate status=504 upstream=connection_reset 
```

maria (oncall): Ops runbook suggests immediate mitigations: 1) Evict low-priority batches 2) Reduce max_batch_size 3) Temporarily enable fallback model variant -> lighter model 4) Scale scheduler. @ops-runbook-bot link?

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: Batch backlog / scheduler saturation: https://runbooks.internal/scheduler-backlog. Suggested cmds: 
- rwdctl scheduler set-eviction --policy=priority --threshold=60%
- rwdctl scheduler config set max_batch_size=16
- rwdctl scale deployment scheduler --replicas +2
- gateway: route fallback traffic to model-quantized-v1

ajay (infra): I'll try scaling first (quickest). Running: ```
rwdctl scale deployment scheduler --replicas 4 --region us-west-2
```

ajay (infra): CLI returned: "scaling scheduler: replicas from 2 -> 4, starting pods". Watching pod startup.

kevin (sre): While new pods spin up, I'd like to reduce batch size to stop adding work to big batches. Maria, can you apply that?

maria (oncall): Applying change: ```
rwdctl scheduler config set max_batch_size=16 --region us-west-2
```

maria (oncall): Config applied. Confirming via metric: avg_batch_size dropped from ~48 -> ~20 over next 30s. Queue ingress still high but per-batch processing time decreased.

alex (support): Customer impact: Support tickets and radar show ~12 customers reporting 502/504s in last 10m. Most are hosted inference endpoints in us-west. Sample IDs: cust-112, cust-889, cust-401. No PII.

lucy (customer-success): Drafting status page update: "We are investigating intermittent 502/504 errors for inference requests in us-west-2. Engineers are actively mitigating; no account data loss. Updates every 15 minutes." Want to post?

maria (oncall): Yes please post that, keep tone accurate. Add note: recommended workaround is to retry with backoff.

ajay (infra): New scheduler pods are Up-> Ready. Throughput increased but we're still seeing some long-tail timeouts. I'm going to toggle the priority eviction to be more aggressive and evict batches older than 30s. ```
rwdctl scheduler set-eviction --policy=age --max-age=30s --region us-west-2
```

ajay (infra): Eviction enabled. Evicting ~270 pending batches. Queue depth dropped by ~55% in the next minute. 5xx rate falling from 18% -> 6% in 3 minutes.

kevin (sre): Great. Also enabling gateway retry-short-circuit to avoid retry storms: ```
gatewayctl set retry_policy --max-retries 1 --short-circuit=true --region us-west-2
```

maria (oncall): I also enabled route fallback to model-quantized-v1 for non-high-priority routes. That reduces load per token. Command: ```
routingctl set-fallback model-quantized-v1 --selector="!priority:high" --region us-west-2
```

sylvia (platform): Noted — fallback activated. Observability: tailing perf traces now show mean latency for fallback traffic ~120ms vs 450ms for stuck batches.

kevin (sre): After scaling + eviction + fallback we're at 2.1% 5xx now and gateway timeouts largely resolved. I'll keep an eye for error regression. Metrics: ```
5xx_rate: 18% -> 6% -> 2.1% over 15m
queue_depth: 1200 -> 540 -> 180
scheduler_cpu: 95% -> 72% -> 48%
```

maria (oncall): Good. @ajay can you check for any recent deploys or config changes that might have triggered this? I see a scheduler optimization landed ~40m before spike (commit: fix/batching-sticky-alloc)

ajay (infra): That commit did change allocation heuristics that can cause longer batch stickiness for long-running requests. I'm rolling it back in us-west-2 temporarily: ```
git revert abcdef123 --apply --namespace scheduler-us-west-2 && rwdctl deploy scheduler --namespace scheduler-us-west-2 --force
```

ajay (infra): Revert deployed. Observing behavior.

kevin (sre): After revert, batch stickiness metric dropped to baseline and average batch duration improved. No regression observed so far.

maria (oncall): Customer update (lucy posted): "We have implemented a mitigation and error rates have reduced significantly. Engineers are continuing to monitor and a post-incident follow-up will be shared." :thumbsup:

ops-runbook-bot: Recommended follow-ups: run full backlog drain verification, enable longer-term autoscaling for scheduler, consider per-customer rate-limits for heavy tenants, schedule postmortem. Link: https://runbooks.internal/scheduler-backlog#post-incident

lucy (customer-success): Some customers asked for ETA. I replied with: "We expect normal service to be restored for most customers within 30-60 minutes; some queued requests may have been dropped and customers may retry. We'll send full postmortem."

maria (oncall): Handing incident to kevin (sre) for longer-term monitoring and postmortem. I'm going offline for ops handover. Key items for postmortem: root cause = scheduler allocation change creating sticky batches + influx of large requests; mitigations = scale + aggressive eviction + fallback + revert commit; customer impact = transient 502/504s for ~40 min, ~12 customers affected.

kevin (sre): Taking it. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. I'll create an incident-brief doc and link it here. Also creating the postmortem ticket.

kevin (sre): Incident brief: https://internaltickets/INC-1789999999. Postmortem assignee: ajay. Action items: 1) Guardrail on batch size change in config PRs (ajay) 2) Autoscales for scheduler sooner (sylvia) 3) Customer-traffic isolation tests (platform + SRE).

maria (oncall): Thanks team. Marking page resolved in PagerDuty. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved by maria (oncall). Auto-close alert in 30m unless reopens.

kevin (sre): Monitoring continues. Will finalize postmortem and link here when ready.

lucy (customer-success): Posted a follow-up to affected customers with summary and workaround notes. No escalations at this time.

maria (oncall): Closing handoff. Back to normal ops.

kevin (sre): Postmortem draft created and shared in #postmortems; link: https://postmortems.internal/1789999999. I'll add timeline and action owner tracking.
